page: Microsoft Azure FX24ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a substantial 260 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 504.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high resource density of 21.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is designated as Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core scores and single-threaded gzip compression rates placing in the top 25% tier. Notably, text processing performance is in the top 10% tier, registering 2,965.0 on Geekbench. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show 2,073.56 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 117.18 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though Passmark memory scores are relatively weak. The instance also exhibits strong performance in static web serving and small-model LLM inference text generation, reaching 420.68 tokens/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated high-frequency Intel Xeon cores, the FX24ms_v2 offers a specialized resource profile. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive memory footprints without needing a proportional scaling of vCPU counts, thereby optimizing licensing costs for memory-bound software. This makes the instance highly suitable for large in-memory databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, heavy text-processing pipelines, and software compilation tasks.
